'''Donald Harry Sadler''' (22 August 1908 – 24 October 1987) was an English astronomer and mathematician
who developed an international reputation for his work in preparing
astronomical and navigational almanacs. He worked as the
[[HM Nautical Almanac Office#Superintendents of the Nautical Almanac|Superintendent of His Majesty's Nautical Almanac Office]] 
from 1937 to 1971.<ref name="obit_qjras">{{cite journal
  | last = Wilkins
  | first = George A.
  | title = Donald Harry Sadler, O.B.E. (1908-1987)
  | journal = [[Quarterly Journal of the Royal Astronomical Society]]
  | volume = 32
  | issue = 1
  | pages = 59–65
  | publisher = [[Royal Astronomical Society]]
  | location = [[London]], [[England]]
  | date = 1991
  | bibcode = 1991QJRAS..32...59W
  }}</ref><ref name="sadler_personal_hist">{{cite web

  | editor-last = Wilkins

  | publisher = United Kingdom Hydrographic Office
  | date = 2008
  | url = http://astro.ukho.gov.uk/nao/history/dhs_gaw
  | access-date = 1 June 2015
}}</ref><ref name="odnb">{{cite ODNB|id=53937|title=Sadler, Donald Harry (1908-1987)|year=2004|last=Wilkins|first=George A.}}</ref>

==Early life==
Donald Sadler was born in [[Dewsbury]], [[Yorkshire]], on 22 August 1908. He
attended the local grammar school where he excelled in mathematics.
He studied mathematics at the [[University of Cambridge]] and received a
first-class degree in 1929.<ref name="obit_qjras"/><ref name="sadler_personal_hist"/>

Sadler developed an interest in celestial mechanics during his studies
at Cambridge. He contributed to the work of the Computing Section of the 
[[British Astronomical Association]].<ref name="obit_qjras"/><ref name="sadler_personal_hist"/>

==The Nautical Almanac Office==
Sadler began work as an assistant at
[[HM Nautical Almanac Office|His Majesty's Nautical Almanac Office]] in 1930,
working under the direction of the
[[HM Nautical Almanac Office#Superintendents of the Nautical Almanac|Superintendent]], 
[[Leslie Comrie]], when it was based at the [[Royal Naval College, Greenwich|Royal Naval College]]
in [[Greenwich]], London. Sadler was promoted to Deputy Superintendent of the Office 
in 1933.<ref name="obit_qjras"/><ref name="sadler_personal_hist"/>

Comrie left the Nautical Almanac Office in 1936. A decision was taken to
move the Office to the [[Royal Observatory, Greenwich]], placing it under 
the direction of the [[Astronomer Royal]], and Sadler was appointed a 
Chief Assistant at the observatory. Sadler was appointed Comrie's successor as
Superintendent of the Nautical Almanac Office in 1937. Sadler was the eighth 
person to occupy this post since it was created in 1818.<ref name="obit_qjras"/>

Sadler took on the task of consolidating projects begun by Comrie,
publishing new tables for use in navigation.
The Second World War soon intervened and the Nautical Almanac Office
was moved temporarily out of London to the safer environment of [[Bath, Somerset|Bath]].
The Office expanded in size temporarily to prepare data for military use.
Sadler was awarded the [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire|OBE]]
in 1948 in recognition of this work.<ref name="obit_qjras"/>

Sadler supervised the relocation of the Nautical Almanac Office
in 1949 from [[Bath, Somerset|Bath]] to the new home of the [[Royal Greenwich Observatory]] 
at [[Herstmonceux Castle]] in Sussex. He expanded the use of calculating
machines in astronomical calculations. He increased international
cooperation in preparing astronomical tables, particularly with the
[[United States Naval Observatory]].<ref name="obit_qjras"/>

In 1954 Sadler married his colleague, [[Flora Sadler]] ([[née]] McBain), in what was described as 'the astronomical romance of the decade'.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The biographical dictionary of Scottish women : from the earliest times to 2004|date=2006|publisher=Edinburgh University Press|others=Ewan, Elizabeth., Innes, Sue., Reynolds, Sian.|isbn=978-0-7486-2660-1|location=Edinburgh|oclc=367680960}}</ref>

Donald Sadler oversaw the transfer of the Nautical Almanac Office within
the Royal Greenwich Observatory from the control of the [[British Admiralty|Admiralty]] 
to the new [[Science Research Council]].<ref name="obit_qjras"/>

==Scientific societies==
Donald Sadler became a fellow of the [[Royal Astronomical Society]] in
1931, and served on the society's council. He acted as a secretary
between 1939 and 1947, contributing to sustaining the society's
work during the war. He served as the society's
[[President of the Royal Astronomical Society|president]] from 1967 
to 1969.<ref name="obit_qjras"/>

Sadler contributed to other scientific societies, including the 
[[Royal Institute of Navigation]], of which he was president from 1953 to 1955.<ref name="InstitutePresidents">{{cite web|url=https://rin.org.uk/page/Pres_and_Dir | title=Presidents and Directors of the RIN |publisher=Royal Institute of Navigation |access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref> He served as general secretary of the [[International Astronomical Union]] (1958–1964), then as vice-president, and president (1968–1970) of the Council of the Federation of Astronomical and Geophysical Services.<ref name="obit_qjras"/>

In 1981, Sadler became a founding member of the [[World Cultural Council]].<ref>{{cite web | title = About Us | publisher = [[World Cultural Council]] | url = http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/about-us/ | access-date = November 8, 2016}}</ref>

==Later life==
Donald Sadler retired as Superintendent of the Nautical Almanac Office in
1971. He continued working at the office for a further year, retiring in
February 1972. Sadler continued with his activities in the 
[[Royal Institute of Navigation]].<ref name="obit_qjras"/><ref name="sadler_personal_hist"/>

Donald Sadler died at [[Bexhill-on-Sea]], [[East Sussex]], on 24 October 1987.<ref name="odnb"/>
